findings.title: tool.press handler references undefined MODIFIER_NAMES — every tool.press call throws ReferenceError and the tab loses focus
findings.boundary: Daemon/orchestrating-agent (bsk) -> Safari persistent background page. tool.press is a daemon-reachable RPC method (background.js:292). It is NOT a cross-trust *data* boundary; it is a correctness/robustness defect at the daemon->extension control boundary that (a) breaks the documented tool set and (b) violates background.js:118-128's own documented invariant that layout-reading ops must not crash and must not act invisibly.
findings.preconditions: Daemon sends `{"method":"tool.press",...}` with any `key` (e.g. Enter, or a `key+Modifier` combo). Verified empirically: dispatching tool.press through real makeBackground() throws `ReferenceError: MODIFIER_NAMES is not defined` (background.js:299). The variable is referenced only at :299 and defined nowhere in the repo (grep over background.js/content.js/protocol.js finds zero other hits). No test dispatches tool.press, so the 19/19 green suite never executes this line — it is dead-on-arrival in production and masked by test coverage.
findings.impact: Two effects. (1) Every tool.press RPC rejects with `protocol_error`/ReferenceError instead of pressing a key, so the tool set README.md:13 advertises as 'working end-to-end' silently fails for keyboard input. (2) Side effect before the throw: defaultTabId (background.js:275,306) already ran `tabs.update(active:true)` + `windows.update(focused:true)`, yanking the human's focus to the agent tab, then the handler dies before `page(tabId,...)` at :301 — so the human gets a focus steal with no keystroke delivered. No privilege escalation and no page/extension-code execution: this is not the 'evaluate escape hatch' red line, just a broken handler + a focus-theft regression.
findings.fix: Define the constant next to the other module-scope constants: add `const MODIFIER_NAMES = ['Control','Alt','Meta','Shift'];` alongside `NO_DIALOGS_KEY` (around background.js:164), or import it from protocol.js. Then destructure it inside makeBackground (background.js:36) like keyToCode, since it is not currently exported. Add one regression test that dispatches `tool.press` with a `Control+a` key to force coverage of this line.
findings.verified_by: grep (only one MODIFIER_NAMES occurrence repo-wide) + Node probe: `bg.dispatch('tool.press',{session_id:'s2',key:'Enter'})` threw ReferenceError at background.js:299.

findings.title: defaultTabId falls back to a global active+currentWindow tab query — a session with no agent window defaults its tool calls onto any tab (including another session's / the human's), and page() activates+focuses that foreign tab first
findings.boundary: Agent-session A -> agent-session B / human browsing context. A tool call addressed to session A (press/navigate/snapshot/scroll_to/screenshot at background.js:249,275,281,287,293,306,312) resolves its tab via defaultTabId, which is NOT bounded by sessionHasTab or s.agentTabIds. This crosses the session-ownership boundary the rest of the file otherwise respects.
findings.preconditions: Session A owns no tab in its own agent window: either the daemon issued no tab_create (session_start only opens an about:blank window whose tabs list can be empty — background.js:177) or it addressed the call with an explicit `tab_id` of a *tab it does not own*. defaultTabId (background.js:107-116) then runs `tabs.query({})`-style fallback: first `{windowId:s.agentWindowId,active:true}`, then `{active:true,currentWindow:true}` over ALL windows/tabs. The windowId-scoped first query is vacuous in practice because `windowId` and `currentWindow`/global-`active` are contradictory filters — an active tab's window is focused, but s.agentWindowId is only focused while the agent's last action focused it. Verified by Node probe: session s2, owning no tab, issued `tool.snapshot` with no tab_id and the op landed on tab 100 (owned by s1/human); `s2.agentTabIds` did not contain it, and the call returned that tab's page text.
findings.impact: Cross-session/cross-context data exposure + interaction: `tool.snapshot` returns an arbitrary foreign tab's page text (session A reads B's / the human's page, e.g. a banking page), and `tool.press`/`tool.scroll_to`/`tool.screenshot` act on a tab A does not own, stealing focus and (for press) typing into the human's or another agent's focused element. In the single-user/single-daemon trust model this is data-leakage/actuation-on-wrong-context, not remote code exec; severity is medium rather than high because exploitation in this deployment requires either a second concurrent session or an out-of-set explicit tab_id, and both operators are the same single daemon-trusted principal.
findings.fix: Bound the fallback to tabs the calling session owns. In defaultTabId, when `s` exists, restrict the fallback query to `s.agentTabIds`/`s.borrowed` keys (or a per-session window filter that actually resolves to owned tabs) instead of `{active:true,currentWindow:true}` over every tab; if a session owns no tab, throw `not_found` like requireSession's siblings rather than borrowing a stranger's tab. Also drop the vacuous `windowId+active` combination (or query `currentWindow` correctly).
findings.verified_by: Node probe against real makeBackground(): s2 (empty agentTabIds) snapshot with no tab_id resolved to tab 100 and returned 'READ-OF-OTHER-TAB'; s2.agentTabIds did not contain it; explicit foreign tab_id paths (249/275) bypass sessionHasTab entirely.

findings.title: tool.tab_close accepts any daemon-supplied tab_id with no session-ownership check (unlike tab_borrow/tab_return/navigate) and activates+focuses the target tab before closing it
findings.boundary: Daemon-reachable RPC -> arbitrary tab lifecycle. tab_borrow (:226) gates on human confirmation, tab_return (:236) and navigate/snapshot/... (:249+) gate on session ownership (requireSession/defaultTabId); tab_close (:212) has neither guard — it closes whatever `p.tab_id` names.
findings.preconditions: Daemon (or any process that impersonated it, see refuted item on Origin-spoofing) issues `tool.tab_close` with an arbitrary `tab_id`. No session_has_tab / agentTabIds membership check is performed. Confirmed by probe: session s2 closed the tab created by session s1, and the cleanup loop removed it from every session's bookkeeping.
findings.impact: Within the accepted model the daemon is already fully trusted (the harness drives Safari to log into sites and fill fields), so arbitrary close is low marginal authority rather than a new escalation. The concrete defects are: (1) it breaks session isolation — session A can close a tab session B owns, and closing a *human* tab has no consent gate (tab_borrow's human-confirmation model does not extend here); (2) activateTab (background.js:124-128) focuses+raises the tab immediately before `tabs.remove`, so closing produces a focus-steal flash even though the tab then dies.
findings.fix: Mirror the ownership discipline used elsewhere: only close a tab after resolving it to the calling session (`if (!s || !(s.agentTabIds.has(p.tab_id) || s.borrowed.has(p.tab_id))) throw {code:'not_found',...}`), or at minimum drop the `activateTab` focus-before-close (close in place / don't focus a tab you are about to destroy).
findings.verified_by: Static read + Node probe: `tool.tab_close` with a foreign session's tab_id closed it (removed from tabs map) and cleaned it from s1.agentTabIds.

findings.title: popup.html injects status() fields into #status via innerHTML (documented deviation from its own 'read-only' comment; not practically exploitable)
findings.boundary: No trust boundary is crossed. popup.html:23 does `el.innerHTML = ...`, which contradicts the comment's claim that the popup is read-only/inert, but the interpolated values (`s.connected`, `s.activeSession` = the newest session_id string, `s.tabCount`) are generated entirely by the extension's own status() (background.js:341-343) and carry no attacker- or page-influenced content.
findings.preconditions: None reachable. To inject markup a page script would have to forge the `bsk-status-request` reply, but that message is only answered by the background listener (background.js:354) and there is no code path by which a content script or page-origin message sets `activeSession`/`tabCount`. So the innerHTML sink has no untrusted source feeding it.
findings.impact: No confidentiality/integrity impact today. Reported only so the 'read-only / inert' claim is not taken as a security property — if a future change ever routes page- or daemon-influenced strings into `status()`, the innerHTML sink becomes a live XSS sink on a chrome-untrusted:// origin. Right now it is a correctness/hygiene nit, not a vulnerability.
findings.fix: Build the status line with textContent (e.g. `el.textContent = 'Daemon: ' + (s.connected?'connected':'NOT connected'); ...` on three lines / a template built with createElement) so the popup stays provably inert even if status() later carries attacker-influenced data.
findings.verified_by: Read popup.html:17-27 + status() (background.js:341-343) and onMessage listener (:345-355): the two values interpolated are extension-generated booleans/strings, not page-influenced.

findings.title: check-notarization.sh / rebuild.sh: docs are accurate and there is NO provisioning-profile or notarization gate to bypass (documentation-divergence hypothesis refuted; no hard-block exists)
findings.boundary: Build/distribution tooling, not a runtime trust boundary. Included to close out hypothesis #6 (doc-vs-enforcement divergence).
findings.preconditions: check-notarization.sh (repo root, present) attempts `xcrun stapler staple` and prints READY/not-ready — it does not gate a build, only informs. rebuild.sh (present) only does the Debug ad-hoc build via safari-web-extension-converter and never invokes codesign/notarytool, so it cannot and does not 'hard-block a missing provisioning profile'. The Developer ID archive/sign/notarize path lives solely in manual NOTES.md:15-48 commands, which pass `PROVISIONING_PROFILE_SPECIFIER=""`.
findings.impact: No divergence and no enforcement gap to report as a vulnerability: NOTES.md/README.md describe check-notarization.sh as a *poll/readiness* tool and describe signing as a manual procedure — they never claim the scripts hard-block anything, so nothing is claimed that isn't enforced. The only observation: neither script enforces the signing/notarization/`--copy-resources` invariants, and `--copy-resources` (NOTES.md:14-16/README Bugs) is a silent-fail footgun that only holds today because of a manual convention (the staging copy lists the needed files explicitly at rebuild.sh:28); a future edit could drop a file and ship an empty Resources/ with no error.
findings.fix: Optional hardening only: if you want a real gate, add a `codesign -dv --verify` / `spctl -a` check (or an `xcrun stapler validate` assert) so a build without a stapled ticket fails loudly, and keep rebuild.sh's explicit file list (rebuild.sh:28) asserted against manifest.json's referenced resources.
findings.verified_by: Read of check-notarization.sh (staple-attempt + echo, exit 1 only when the .app dir is absent) and rebuild.sh (Debug-only build, no signing step).

refuted: H1 (protocol.js parseFrames): REFUTED — there is no parseFrames function anywhere in the repo (grep over all JS/MD returns zero hits). protocol.js exposes only handshakeParams/NO_DIALOGS/keyToCode/keyToModifiers/rpcOk/rpcErr. The closest thing to 'frame handling' is background.js:78 `ws.onmessage = (e)=>handleFrame(JSON.parse(e.data))`: JSON.parse of malformed JSON throws OUTSIDE handleFrame, so it rejects onmessage's promise and is not routed through dispatch's rpcErr path (:85); it does NOT call socket.close. A malformed frame can therefore only (a) be silently dropped (handled method -> dispatch -> rpcOk/rpcErr) or (b) leave a hanging, unanswered call on the daemon if an id'd event frame throws on JSON.parse. So the hypothesized 'throw -> socket.close -> disconnect' fail-closed behavior does not exist in source.

H2 (second session borrows a LIVE session's tab without its consent): REFUTED — tool.tab_borrow (background.js:223-232) unconditionally requires human confirmation via requestBorrowConfirmation (:226) before it will mark ANY tab borrowed, and it never consults/mutates another session's `borrowed` map (no sessionHasTab/ownership guard exists — the premise's 'sessionHasTab' is a real symbol nowhere in the source). The only per-tab ownership concept (agentTabIds/borrowed) is written by session_start, never consulted to block reassignment. Net: you cannot reassign a live session's tab without an explicit human click, and the confirm popup (focused:true) + activateTab focus-steal make concurrent-session interference visible rather than silent.

H4 (evaluate escape hatch): REFUTED — no tool.evaluate handler exists. dispatch (background.js:323-327) throws {code:'unsupported'} for any method not in the tools{} map (background.js:167-321); evaluate is explicitly listed in README.md:13 and NOTES.md as returning a clean 'unsupported' error. No `eval(`, `new Function`, or `extension.getURL`-based arbitrary-code sink exists anywhere (grep: NONE). The tools map implements exactly the reduced set session/tab/navigate/snapshot/click/fill/press/scroll_to/screenshot; nothing in it feeds arbitrary page JS or arbitrary extension-page JS to an executeScript/eval sink.

H5a (confirm can be answered by a non-user principal / second daemon connection): REFUTED (recorded as a strength) — the only producer of a 'borrow-confirm-result' message is confirm.js:7 (the human clicking Allow/Deny in a focused popup). content.js's onMessage listener (content.js:144-148) matches ops[m.op] (snapshot/click/fill/press/scrollTo/viewportSize) and never emits 'borrow-confirm-result'. The background onMessage listener (background.js:345-355) never inspects msg.sender, but there is no daemon-to-content-script relay and no second-daemon-channel that could forge it; the daemon can only *send tool calls*, and its own connection carries no tab-content script message into confirm's flow. The confirmation gate (and its timeout-to-deny at :159) is therefore human-in-the-loop and fail-closed — no non-user principal can answer it.

H5b (confirm result-shape vs page() result contract): REFUTED as an incompatibility — they are two independent channels, so no shape mismatch exists. page() (background.js:130-138) is for tool ops and checks res.ok/res.error; the borrow-confirmation round trip is a separate message whose reply is consumed at background.js:346-349, which consumes msg.allow (truthy) and does NOT expect the content-script {ok,...} envelope. The test background.test.mjs:165 even pins 'exactly one onMessage listener', confirming the two message types deliberately share a listener without a contract clash.

H6 (docs claim a provisioning-profile hard-block the scripts don't enforce): REFUTED — check-notarization.sh and rebuild.sh are both present at the repo root (confirmed via find/ls). Neither script is documented or coded as a provisioning-profile/notarization *gate*: check-notarization.sh polls stapler readiness and rebuild.sh is a Debug ad-hoc build (no signing step). NOTES.md/README.md never claim the scripts hard-block a missing profile, so there is nothing documented-but-unenforced to report.

InnerHTML sweep: only ONE innerHTML sink exists — popup.html:23. background.js, confirm.js, content.js, and confirm.html contain no innerHTML (confirm.js/confirm.html use textContent for title/url). The popup sink is reported above as an informational deviation and is not attacker-reachable.
